html:
SMTO-HTTP-0001 — This sign-in method isn't available on the Gateway

GUID: 105b9226-dec8-425e-bcae-12c15e0a2cc8
Slug: http-auth-provider-unavailable
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • This HTTP Connection uses a sign-in method, such as NTLM or Negotiate (Kerberos), that the Gateway computer can't load. SMTO stopped before sending your request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select this HTTP Connection, and note which sign-in method is chosen under Authentication. NTLM and Negotiate need extra software on the Gateway computer; the other types don't.
  2. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to run the Gateway installer again on that computer, as the account the Gateway runs under, then restart the Gateway once its current work has finished. The installer adds the missing sign-in software without removing the Gateway's pairing or settings.
  3. If the service also accepts another sign-in method, choose it under Authentication instead, fill in its settings and save. A built-in sign-in method works without any extra software on the Gateway.
  4. Select Test connection for this HTTP Connection. The test signs in through the Gateway and shows whether the method now loads.

What success looks like

  • Test connection reports Reachable and Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't delete the Gateway or its saved sign-in details to fix this; the installer repairs it in place, and granting a Skill permission won't install the missing software.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The HTTP authentication type is not in the Gateway's provider registry, or its optional enterprise handler (requests_ntlm, requests_gssapi or requests_negotiate_sspi) failed to import or load its native libraries.

What this means

  • The requested authentication type is absent from the provider registry, or an optional enterprise provider raises ImportError/OSError while loading. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The requested authentication type is absent from the provider registry, or an optional enterprise provider raises ImportError/OSError while loading.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish an unsupported provider name from a missing or unloadable NTLM/Negotiate package before changing credentials.

How to fix it

  • For NTLM or Negotiate, repair the Gateway in place by rerunning its installer as the account the Gateway runs under (./install.sh for the Server plus local Gateway, or ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows); Negotiate also needs OS Kerberos or SSPI credentials on that host. After active work settles, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata. If the auth type itself is unsupported, change the profile to a supported provider; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials or settings.
  • Inspect the authentication method. If an NTLM or Negotiate package is missing or cannot load, reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata. An unsupported authentication method instead requires selecting a supported provider; credentials remain a separate prerequisite.
  • If installation repair is indicated: From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After an installation repair: After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected supported provider loads on the actual Gateway and connection readiness passes.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
